pensionTaxCredit.title: Pension Savings & IRP Tax Credit Calculator
pensionTaxCredit.subtitle: For tax year {year}. See how much tax you save by adding to a pension savings account or IRP before December 31, and what tax you pay when you withdraw later.
pensionTaxCredit.salaryHint: With salary income only: 16.5% if gross salary is ₩55M or less, 13.2% above that (local income tax included). With other income, the test is total income of ₩45M.
pensionTaxCredit.psHint: What you have paid since January plus scheduled transfers through December. Pension savings (funds, insurance) count up to ₩6M.
pensionTaxCredit.irpHint: Only money you paid in yourself. Severance pay moved into an IRP and employer pension contributions do not qualify.
pensionTaxCredit.isaHint: Amount moved (or to be moved) from a matured ISA into a pension account within 60 days of maturity. In that year only, the limit rises by 10% of the transfer (up to ₩3M).

isaTo.label: Transferred into
isaTo.hint: The transfer counts as a payment that year, so it first fills the regular limit of the account it goes into. In a pension savings account the ₩6M cap still applies.

result.label: Tax saved this year with pension savings and IRP
result.detail: Eligible ₩{base} × {rate}%, within this year's tax of ₩{tax} estimated from salary alone (local income tax included).
result.none: Nothing paid in yet. Each won you pay cuts tax by {rate}%, up to the tax you owe.

limit.over: ₩{over} above the limit is not credited this year. From next year you can ask the financial company to convert it into that year's payment (Income Tax Act Enforcement Decree Art. 118-3).

topUp.title: If you add more by December 31
topUp.desc: You have ₩{room} of limit left this year. Move the slider to try an amount.
topUp.result: Paying ₩{amt} more cuts tax by another ₩{gain}, for ₩{total} in total this year. The money itself stays in your pension account.
topUp.zero: Pick an amount to see the extra refund.
topUp.split: Counted as ₩{ps} to pension savings + ₩{irp} to IRP (pension savings only counts up to ₩6M, the rest goes to IRP).
topUp.full: You have used this year's limit (₩6M pension savings, ₩9M combined). Extra payments are not credited this year, but can be converted into a later year's payment.
topUp.yearEnd: Calculate the full year-end refund with these payments

cap.title: Part of this won't increase your refund
cap.body: This year's tax from salary alone is ₩{tax} (incl. local tax), so eligible payments above ₩{useful} no longer reduce tax. In this plan, ₩{wasted} has no tax effect.
cap.tip: Card spending and dependant deductions lower your tax further, so this threshold drops. Leave the ineffective part out of your year-end claim: it stays an uncredited payment you can convert into a later year's payment (Decree Art. 118-3) or withdraw tax-free later with a deduction confirmation (Decree Art. 201-10).

deadline.note: Only money deposited by December 31, {year} counts for this year. December 31 is a stock market holiday every year and cut-off times differ by company; some move the IRP cut-off to the afternoon of the last business day. Check your provider's notice and pay in a few days early.

later.title: Tax when you withdraw later
later.desc: Credited payments (₩{base}) and their investment gains are taxed when withdrawn: 3.3–5.5% as a pension after 55, 16.5% if you cancel early.
later.caption: Tax refunded this year vs tax paid on withdrawal
later.loss: Cancelling early costs ₩{tax} in other-income tax, more than the ₩{refund} refunded this year: a ₩{loss} loss. The 16.5% exit rate is higher than your credit rate, or gains and payments that had no tax effect are taxed too.
later.even: Cancelling early pays back the ₩{refund} refunded this year as ₩{tax} exit tax, so you break even. Taken as a pension after 55, the tax drops to ₩{annuity} (under 70).
notes: To receive it as a pension you must be 55+, have held the account 5 years, apply to start payments, and withdraw within the yearly limit (account value ÷ (11 − payout year) × 120%) (Decree Art. 40-2(3)).

If private pension income (credited principal and gains, excluding severance taken as a pension) is ₩15M or less a year, 3.3–5.5% is final. Above that you choose between comprehensive taxation of the full amount and 16.5% separate taxation, so spreading payouts to stay under ₩15M helps (Income Tax Act Art. 14(3)9, Art. 64-4).

Even an early withdrawal is taxed at the pension rate (3.3–5.5%) instead of 16.5% for unavoidable reasons proven within 6 months: natural disaster, death or emigration, 3+ months of medical care for you or a dependant, bankruptcy or rehabilitation (Decree Art. 20-2).
Partial withdrawals take uncredited payments out first, and those are tax-free (Decree Art. 40-3).
The lifetime annuity rate is 3.3% (was 4.4%) for pensions received from January 1, 2026. If an age rate also applies, the lower one is used (Income Tax Act Art. 129(1)5-2).

guide.title: Pension account tax credit essentials (tax year {year})
items: Rate: 15% of payments if gross salary is ₩55M or less (total income ₩45M or less if you have other income), 12% above that. With local income tax: 16.5% and 13.2% (Income Tax Act Art. 59-3(1)).
Limit: ₩6M a year for pension savings, ₩9M combined with IRP. To use the full ₩9M, split e.g. ₩6M pension savings + ₩3M IRP, or put ₩9M into an IRP.
Payments into your own account reduce only your own tax. Dual-income couples can each claim ₩9M, and each person's rate depends on their own salary.
You can pay in up to ₩18M a year across pension accounts (ISA transfers are extra). Payments above the credit limit can be converted into a later year's payment (Decree Arts. 40-2(2), 118-3).
Moving a matured ISA into a pension account within 60 days raises that year's limit by 10% of the transfer (up to ₩3M), for up to ₩12M (Income Tax Act Art. 59-3(4), Decree Art. 118-2(3)).
Severance pay moved into an IRP and transfers from other pension accounts are not new payments and are not credited (Income Tax Act Art. 59-3(1)).
Only deposits made by December 31 count for this year. Payment records appear in Hometax's simplified year-end data the following January.
If your determined tax is zero, the credit refunds nothing. This calculator estimates tax from salary alone; if you have many card or dependant deductions, check with the year-end tax calculator.
guide.assume: Assumptions: salary income only, with the personal deduction and 2026 social insurance rates; no card or other deductions. Tax by salary uses the same formulas as the year-end tax calculator. Pension products can lose principal.
